rows.title: 多尺度可編程車體與形態記憶極限 5/90 MULTISCALE PROGRAMMABLE VEHICLE BODIES AND MORPHOLOGICAL MEMORY AT THE LIMIT MULTISCALE PROGRAMMABLE VEHICLE BODIES AND MORPHOLOGICAL MEMORY AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page high-density English research working monograph exploring whether multiscale programmable vehicle-body materials can retain and reconstruct morphological history while switching reversibly between safe, measurable shapes. It studies shape-memory polymers, bistable mechanical cells, geometry-memory records, thermal activation and structural reliability without assuming that visible shape recovery establishes load-bearing integrity. Its central claim is falsifiable. Under equal material, energy, time, sensing, control and analysis budgets, a preregistered programmable system should improve unselected structural yield without worsening joint slip against fixed monocoque and passive modular-lattice benchmarks. The claim fails if gains come from passive relaxation, hidden heating or selection of favorable specimens, if forward/reverse work and internal state cannot be reconstructed, or if any physical safety stop is violated. Thirty distinct mathematical plates address morphing work, cycle hysteresis, shape fixation and recovery, thermomechanical strain partition, temperature-dependent constitutive laws, state kinetics, thermal conduction, elastic buckling, multistability, viscoelasticity, topology, uncertainty, observable memory states and conjunctive release. Each identifies assumptions, measurement units and a blinded falsification condition. Across 82 chapters and 410 independent single-page research studies, the book examines programmable materials, memory-state identifiability, fatigue, thermal gradients, geometric fidelity, distributed control and cross-laboratory reproduction. Two hundred Research Gates offer individually specified scientific challenges, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinguishable scientific artifacts and next-generation experiments. This work is a prospective, non-occupancy research architecture. It reports no completed vehicle experiments or passenger safety certification. Unobserved load paths, incomplete state identification, progressive joint release or unbounded thermal and stored-energy exposure trigger withholding and stop. The goal is a reproducible research contract, not a promise of technological readiness.
